evidence: $1.20 per share (the "Original Issue Price"), based on a pre-money valuation of $48,000,000 on a fully diluted basis (40,000,000 shares)

also.source: Series A Preferred Stock Purchase Agreement - Draft 3 (November 10, 2026)
also.evidence: at a purchase price of $1.20 per share (the "Original Issue Price")

also.source: Board consent approving the Series A financing (signed November 12, 2026)

question: what's the pre-money on the Northlake Series A, and on what basis is it calculated?
source: Series A term sheet - Northlake Analytics / Granite Peak (signed September 24, 2026)
clause: Price Per Share; Fully Diluted Basis; Option Pool
evidence: based on a pre-money valuation of $48,000,000 on a fully diluted basis (40,000,000 shares) and a post-money valuation of $60,000,000 (50,000,000 shares). | The pre-money valuation counts all outstanding Common Stock, all outstanding Series Seed Preferred Stock on an as-converted basis, all outstanding options and an unallocated option pool equal to 12% of the post-money fully diluted capitalization.
note: $48,000,000 on a fully diluted basis (40,000,000 shares at $1.20), counting all outstanding Common, the Series Seed Preferred as converted, outstanding options and an unallocated pool equal to 12% of the post-money capitalization (6,000,000 shares), so the pool increase is borne by the existing holders. Post-money is $60,000,000 (50,000,000 shares).

question: What liquidation preference does the Series A get, and is it participating?
source: Series A term sheet - Northlake Analytics / Granite Peak (signed September 24, 2026)
evidence: the greater of (i) one times (1x) the Original Issue Price plus any declared but unpaid dividends and (ii) the amount they would receive if their shares had been converted into Common Stock. The Series A Preferred is non-participating
note: 1x the Original Issue Price ($1.20 a share) plus declared but unpaid dividends, or the as-converted amount if greater; non-participating, paid pari passu with the Series Seed and ahead of the Common. Dividends are 6% non-cumulative, only if declared.

question: How much of Pell Strand's fees does Northlake have to pay at closing?
source: Series A Preferred Stock Purchase Agreement - Draft 3 (November 10, 2026)
evidence: the Company shall pay, at the Initial Closing, the reasonable fees and expenses of Pell Strand LLP, counsel for the Purchasers, not to exceed $45,000.

also.source: Series A term sheet - Northlake Analytics / Granite Peak (signed September 24, 2026)
also.evidence: The Company will pay at the Closing the reasonable fees and expenses of one counsel to the Investors, Pell Strand LLP, up to $50,000.

note: The documents conflict. SPA Draft 3 Section 6.9 caps the Company's payment of Pell Strand's reasonable fees and expenses at the Initial Closing at $45,000; the signed term sheet says up to $50,000, and its Expenses section is one of the three binding provisions. Once signed, the SPA supersedes the term sheet (6.14), but expect Pell Strand to ask for $50,000. Flag it to the client before the draft goes final.

question: Is the closing deadline in the SPA draft consistent with the term sheet?
source: Series A Preferred Stock Purchase Agreement - Draft 3 (November 10, 2026)
evidence: This Agreement may be terminated by the Company or the Lead Investor if the Initial Closing has not occurred by December 31, 2026.

also.source: Series A term sheet - Northlake Analytics / Granite Peak (signed September 24, 2026)
also.evidence: Closing expected on or before December 15, 2026.

also.source: Email from Granite Peak (Rafael Mendes) about the closing (November 13, 2026)
also.evidence: We would like to keep the December 15 target from the term sheet.

note: No. The term sheet says closing is expected on or before December 15, 2026, and Rafael Mendes's email of November 13, 2026 asks to keep that target. SPA Draft 3 Section 6.4 sets an Outside Date of December 31, 2026 (termination right for the Company or the Lead Investor). The term sheet date is an expectation, not a deadline, but the draft should be aligned with the client and Granite Peak. The actual closing date is not yet fixed.

question: Run a definitions check on SPA Draft 3: is "Knowledge" defined consistently?
source: Series A Preferred Stock Purchase Agreement - Draft 3 (November 10, 2026)
evidence: "Knowledge," including the phrase "to the Company's knowledge," means the actual knowledge of Priya Raman, Owen Fitzgerald and Laura Chen, after reasonable inquiry. | For purposes of this Section 2, "Knowledge" (including the phrase "to the Company's knowledge") means the actual knowledge of Priya Raman and Owen Fitzgerald, without inquiry.
note: No. "Knowledge" is defined twice, differently. Section 1.3: the actual knowledge of Priya Raman, Owen Fitzgerald and Laura Chen, after reasonable inquiry. Section 2 lead-in: the actual knowledge of Priya Raman and Owen Fitzgerald, without inquiry. The Section 2 version governs the representations (narrower: no Laura Chen, no inquiry), which the Purchasers will resist; one definition should be deleted.

question: Is Juniper a Major Investor under the IRA? Does it get information and pro rata rights?
evidence: "Major Investor" means any Investor that, individually or together with its Affiliates, holds at least 1,000,000 shares of Series A Preferred Stock … Shares of Series Seed Preferred Stock and Common Stock are not counted toward this threshold. | Juniper Seed Partners, L.P. | Attention: Ben Okoro | 833,333 | 4,000,000

also.source: Series A term sheet - Northlake Analytics / Granite Peak (signed September 24, 2026)
also.evidence: A "Major Investor" is an Investor holding at least 1,000,000 shares of Series A Preferred.
Juniper Seed Partners, L.P. | Series A Preferred | - | - | 833,333 | 833,333 | 1.67%

note: No. A Major Investor must hold at least 1,000,000 shares of Series A Preferred; Juniper buys only 833,333, and its 4,000,000 Series Seed shares do not count (IRA 1.8). So Juniper gets neither the information rights (3.1) nor the right of first offer (4.1). Granite Peak (6,666,667) and Halcyon (2,500,000) are Major Investors. Juniper would need 166,667 more Series A shares.
